title: Election Commission of India & Electoral Reforms
summary: Constitutional provisions under Article 324, composition, powers, and RPA 1950 vs 1951 comparison.

relationships.label: RBI Grade B 2024 Question on ECI Powers

blocks.content: The Election Commission of India (ECI) is a permanent, autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at national and state levels.

blocks.title: Superintendence, Direction & Control
blocks.summary: Article 324 grants all-encompassing electoral authority over Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President & Vice-President.
details: ECI does NOT conduct elections for Panchayats and Municipalities (managed by State Election Commissions under Art 243K/243ZA).
Multi-member body since 1993 comprising Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and 2 Election Commissioners (ECs).

blocks.title: Exam Trap: Removal Procedure Differentiation
blocks.content: The CEC can be removed from office ONLY in like manner and on like grounds as a Supreme Court Judge. However, Election Commissioners can be removed by the President ONLY on the recommendation of the CEC.
blocks.trapDetails: Do not confuse the removal of CEC (requires Parliamentary impeachment-like process) with ECs (requires CEC recommendation).

events.title: Establishment of ECI
events.description: ECI established as a single-member body with Sukumar Sen as first CEC.

events.title: First Expansion
events.description: Converted to 3-member body following lowering of voting age from 21 to 18 (61st Constitutional Amendment Act).

events.title: Permanent Multi-Member Status
events.description: Multi-member structure institutionalized with equal decision-making powers among CEC and ECs.
